title: Instantaneous versus average velocity
canonical_question: What is the difference between instantaneous and average velocity?
summary: Average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time for a trip.
The two are equal only when the velocity is constant throughout.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Now versus over a stretch
sections.body_md: Average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time for a trip. Instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a single moment, what the speedometer shows. A journey can have a modest average yet high instantaneous values along the way.

sections.heading: When they agree
sections.body_md: The two are equal only when the velocity is constant throughout. Whenever speed or direction changes, the instantaneous value drifts above or below the average. Distinguishing them avoids mistakes in motion problems.

key_points: Average velocity is displacement over total time.
Instantaneous velocity is the value at one instant.
They match only for constant velocity.
core.bridge_to_parent: It contrasts two velocity measures under the objective.
